synthesis.body: When an exception class gates a DESTRUCTIVE action, give the reader a typed hierarchy rather than matching on the message. loop-engine decided whether to delete `events.pending` — a durable audit record — by testing `str(exc)` against a hand-listed set of message fragments, duplicated at two call sites. The list had already fallen behind the reader it mirrored: it omitted the non-finite-number message, so a NaN or 1e400 in events.pending was never recognised as invalid content and the file was retained forever, re-warning on every transition. The fix is a `ManagedContentError(ValueError)` raised at the content sites plus one isinstance-based helper. "The bytes are unusable" and "the read failed" are different facts, and only the first may authorise a delete. Subclassing ValueError kept every existing `except` clause working unchanged, so the migration was additive. Pairs with the catch-broadly-act-narrowly topic: the same line needs a broad catch and a narrow typed predicate.

title: Type the exception that authorises a destructive action — never match its message
